clue.text: Support, also, amended motion

parts.note: a prop is something that holds up or supports

indicators.note: amended means changed, so the letters of also are rearranged

explanation.surface: A committee member backs a motion and also a change to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make 'also' read as a link, but it is the fodder 'amended' works on (giving OSAL), and 'motion' means a formal suggestion, not movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion put to a meeting is a formal suggestion for debate, a synonym.

clue.text: Faith that's left one, in part

indicators.note: in puts the left and one letters inside the word for part

parts.note: a region is a part of a country

explanation.surface: A belief that someone partly abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A faith is a system of belief and worship, a synonym.

clue.text: PM, ie Prime Minister, initially, does it incorrectly

indicators.note: incorrectly means these letters are put together the wrong way, so rearranged
initially takes just the opening letter of Minister

explanation.surface: A note about the Prime Minister getting something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like Prime Minister but is the afternoon abbreviation; 'ie' is a link. 'incorrectly' rearranges PRIME, M and DOES IT.
explanation.definitionFit: PM abbreviates the Latin for after midday, used in giving afternoon times.

clue.text: Became bitter about a volume much enjoyed

indicators.note: about means the word for became bitter goes round the other letters

parts.note: soured means turned sour or bitter

explanation.surface: Someone grew resentful over a book everyone else loved.
explanation.definitionFit: To savour something is to relish and enjoy it fully.

clue.text: Works in foreign stock exchange, mostly

parts.note: la Bourse is the French name for the Paris stock exchange

explanation.definitionFit: Labours are pieces of hard work or toil, as in the labours of Hercules.

clue.text: End of Socrates, over time, seen as disgrace

indicators.note: over here means spanning, so the Greek letter goes round the time abbreviation

parts.note: in Greek the philosopher's name ends in the letter sigma, the Greek S

explanation.surface: The death of the philosopher, long ago, was viewed as shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of Socrates' suggests his death by hemlock, but it means the Greek letter that ends his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame or social disgrace.

clue.text: Rush an expression of grief? Doesn't sound like it

definitions.meaning: to rush is to dash or race along at speed
a drop from the eye shed when crying

explanation.surface: Is a teardrop really a sprint? The spoken words differ.
explanation.walkthrough: One spelling, two pronunciations: the dash rhymes with care, the drop rhymes with fear, which is what 'Doesn't sound like it' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeding along and a drop of eye moisture share one spelling but differ in pronunciation.

clue.text: Troops oddly surly, including veteran

indicators.note: including means the odd letters go round the word for veteran
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of surly

parts.note: an oldie is an old person, a veteran

explanation.surface: Bad-tempered soldiers include an old-timer.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiery means soldiers collectively, a body of troops.

clue.text: Struck back when trapped by a tyrant, ignoble character

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside, so the turned word goes within the other pieces

parts.note: Nero was the notoriously tyrannical Roman emperor

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for struck in the opposite direction

parts.note: struck means hit

explanation.surface: Someone hit back when caught by a despot, showing their low nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struck back' reads as retaliation; here 'back' just turns the synonym round (TIH), and 'when trapped by' houses it in the tyrant phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist lacking heroic, noble qualities is the standard sense of the term.

clue.text: Woeful expression, in isolated state, cut off

indicators.note: cut off means the end of the state's name is chopped away

parts.note: Alaska is the US state cut off from the other mainland states

explanation.surface: Someone sighs sadly while stranded in a remote place with no contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' removes the last two letters, KA, from ALASKA.

clue.text: However unrefined, bishop and cardinal of highest quality

rough means crude or unrefined
B is the chess notation for bishop
cardinal is a shade of red, after the robes of cardinals

explanation.surface: Clergymen, a bishop and a cardinal, are judged first-rate though coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Used of a pedigree horse, then figuratively of anything first-class and well bred.

clue.text: Taking a look at fliers ready to be photographed?

definitions.text: Taking a look at fliers ready to be photographed?

parts.words: Taking a look at fliers ready to be photographed?
parts.note: observing wild fowl, with a nod to the photographer's 'watch the birdie' said before taking a picture

explanation.surface: Someone eyes leaflets or aviators about to have their picture taken.
explanation.walkthrough: Photographers used to tell sitters to 'watch the birdie'; fliers are birds, not leaflets or pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: The hobby is observing wild fowl in their natural habitat.

clue.text: Ship covering area, following straight path

indicators.note: covering means the ship's word wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A vessel sweeping across a region keeps to a straight course.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means arranged in or moving along a straight line.

clue.text: Had row, say, then changed gear, hence driver's anger

indicators.note: say signals that we want a word pronounced like rowed

parts.note: had a row means argued, rowed (rhyming with cowed)

indicators.note: changed means the letters of gear are rearranged

explanation.surface: After an argument a motorist crunches the gears and loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: ROWED in its quarrelling sense rhymes with loud, but the clue needs it pronounced like a boat being rowed, sounding like ROAD; 'changed' turns GEAR into RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury that erupts in motorists at other traffic is the familiar term for this.

clue.text: Relaxes in sun, perturbed about breeze

parts.note: a wind is a breeze

explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to loosen up and let tension go, a synonym.

clue.text: Analysed what's in case

taking the contents out of a suitcase, describing the emptied items

explanation.surface: A detective examines the contents of a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysed means broken down and explained; luggage contents are taken out after travel.

clue.text: River vessel, in past, as local supplier

indicators.note: in places the river and vessel inside the word for past

explanation.surface: A boat on the river was, in former times, how goods reached the area.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub, which a brewery supplies with beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewery makes the beer sold in pubs, and the local is one's neighbourhood pub.

clue.text: Wine with rum primarily, namely mixed drink

clue.text: Rule covering fool put in new position

clue.text: Not positive it's part of the New Testament?

clue.text: Disciplined form of wordplay I discarded

clue.text: Not lying through one's teeth? Not entirely

clue.text: Parent drunk? Something to do with gin

clue.text: Somehow clothe woman, covering maiden such as Virginia

clue.text: Blocks out or cuts into view coming back
